mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal from accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sharp INDPRO drop, indicating the supply shock is not reliably negative for equities.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as an increase of > 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakening is not negatively impacting consumer sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, defined as the spread between the 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields falling below 50 basis points, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed cuts the federal funds rate by > 50bps within the next 3 months, reversing the implied monetary tightening signal from the flattening yield curve.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts, defined as a year-over-year increase of > 20% in the HOUST index, signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate rises by > 100bps in the month following the HOUST surge, indicating the housing strength is not sustainable.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in payroll employment, defined as a month-over-month decline of > 200,000 jobs in the PAYEMS series, signals a sudden labor market shock that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) fall by > 10% in the week following the PAYEMS drop, indicating the labor market shock is not as severe as initially signaled.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the consumer price index, defined as a year-over-year increase of > 4% in the CPIAUCSL index, signals a wage-price spiral that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (CES0500000003) rise by > 5% YoY in the month following the CPIAUCSL trigger, indicating wages are keeping pace with inflation and mitigating the negative impact on real consumer spending power.

mechanism_narrative: A collapse in consumer sentiment, defined as a month-over-month drop of > 10 points in the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index (UMCSENT), signals a sudden shift in consumer behavior that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) rise by > 1% MoM in the month following the UMCSENT drop, indicating the collapse in sentiment is not translating into reduced consumer spending.
